seo.title: How to Set Up Apple Business for Apple Maps
seo.meta_description: How Anaheim and Orange County businesses can set up Apple Business, formerly Apple Business Connect, and verify their organization for Apple Maps.

h1: How to Set Up Apple Business to Manage Your Apple Maps Listing
answer: To set up Apple Business, go to business.apple.com, sign up, then verify your organization with two methods, such as a D-U-N-S Number or EIN plus a business document, within 60 days. Apple Business replaced Apple Business Connect and lets you manage how your business appears in Apple Maps, Siri and Wallet. For Anaheim and Orange County businesses, it reaches iPhone users who never open Google Maps.
key_takeaways: Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business.
Verification uses two methods and can take up to five business days.
Your listing appears in Maps, Siri, Wallet and more.

sections.heading: Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business
sections.body_html: Apple's guide states that Apple Business Connect is now Apple Business, which combines what was previously in Apple Business Manager, Apple Business Essentials and Apple Business Connect into one offering. If you used Apple Business Connect before, you can sign in to Apple Business with the same personal Apple Account.

sections.heading: Why Apple Maps matters locally
sections.body_html: Many iPhone users search for businesses in Apple Maps, ask Siri for directions or tap a place in Messages or Calendar. Apple's guide says the place card appears in many parts of Apple's software, from Maps to Siri to Calendar and Messages. For a business in Anaheim or anywhere in Orange County, an accurate Apple listing reaches customers Google can't.

sections.heading: Sign up
sections.body_html: Go to business.apple.com and select Get Started. You'll enter your organization's details, verify your email and phone number with codes, and agree to the Apple Business terms and conditions.

sections.heading: Coming from Apple Business Connect
sections.body_html: Apple says you can sign in with the personal Apple Account you used for Apple Business Connect. You can create an Apple Account for Work, a Managed Apple Account with the full feature set, or keep your personal Apple Account and use only the brand and location management features.

sections.heading: Verify your organization
sections.body_html: Apple says organizations have 60 days to verify, using two verification methods, and that verification can take up to five business days, longer at busy times. In Apple Business, choose Settings, then Organization, then Verify Now.

sections.heading: Verification methods
sections.body_html:
• Business ID: a D-U-N-S Number or Employer Identification Number (EIN).
  • Domain validation: add a TXT record to your DNS.
  • App Store Connect, if you have an app (not available to third-party partners or agencies).
  • Upload an official document: business license, sales tax permit, food, health or alcohol permit, lease or property agreement, utility bill, or other.

sections.heading: Agencies and partners
sections.body_html: Apple's guide notes that third-party partners and agencies also verify their organization and can manage locations on behalf of clients. If an agency manages your listing, make sure your business still has its own access.

sections.heading: What to do after verification
sections.body_html:
1. Add or claim your location.
  2. Upload your logo and a cover photo.
  3. Complete hours, categories, phone and website.
  4. Add Actions such as booking or ordering.
  5. Create a showcase for current offers.
  6. Check insights monthly.

sections.heading: Apple Business and Google Business Profile
sections.body_html: They're separate. Your Google Business Profile controls Google Search and Maps; Apple Business controls Apple Maps and other Apple apps. Keep the name, address, phone, hours and website identical in both.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Assuming Google listings also update Apple Maps.
  • Missing the 60-day verification window.
  • Using a personal account nobody else in the business can access.
  • Blocking emails from apple.com domains, so verification messages are missed.
  • Leaving an agency as the only account holder.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether Apple Business costs anything to set up. Apple doesn't describe a fee for managing locations in the pages we checked; ads on Maps are a separate, paid option with their own budget. Another common question is whether a business already appears on Apple Maps without signing up. Many do, from Apple's data and partners, but you can't control the details until you claim and verify. Owners also ask how long the whole process takes. Organization verification can take up to five business days, and individual items such as photos and showcases are reviewed by Apple, so plan a week or two to get everything live. Starting early, before a busy season, is the safest approach.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Signed up at business.apple.com.
  • Organization verified with two methods.
  • Business controls the account.
  • Location claimed.
  • Photos and logo uploaded.
  • Details match Google Business Profile.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a family dental practice in Fullerton that has a strong Google Business Profile but has never touched Apple Maps, where its hours are out of date. The office manager signs up for Apple Business, verifies with the practice's EIN and a utility bill, claims the location, fixes the hours and uploads a logo and cover photo. iPhone users asking Siri for a nearby dentist now see accurate details.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: This task is one piece of a wider local plan. Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity, so the profile, your website and your reputation all have to agree. A practical order for most Orange County businesses is: get the Business Profile verified and accurate, make the name, address and phone identical everywhere, publish one clear page per service, then build a steady habit of genuine reviews and replies. Each step makes the next one work better, and the same signals help AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI features describe your business correctly when someone in Anaheim asks for a recommendation.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Sign up at business.apple.com.
  2. Gather your EIN or D-U-N-S Number and a business document.
  3. Submit verification.
  4. Allow mail from apple.com domains.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Most of this can be done in-house with an hour or two and careful reading of Google's own help pages. It is worth bringing in help when the stakes are high or the problem keeps coming back: a profile that has been suspended more than once, many locations to manage, a site that keeps failing the same checks, or no time to keep up the routine. A good local SEO partner should explain what they will change and why, point to Google's guidelines rather than promise rankings, and leave you with access to every account. Chimera works this way with businesses across Anaheim and Orange County.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Sign up at business.apple.com, verify your organization with two methods within 60 days, then complete your location, photos and Actions. Chimera, based in Anaheim, sets up Apple Business for Orange County businesses alongside their Google profiles.
